{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Nineteen rules were assessed: **six require redlines** (three critical, one high, two medium, one low, including two clauses that are simply absent), and **thirteen sit at or above our preferred or fallback positions and are not being touched**.

The risk profile is heavily one-sided. Three points drive the negotiation:

- **Risk allocation is inverted.** TrueLink's only indemnity is for its own breach, with no duty to defend and no IP, data-breach or misconduct cover, while Client gives a very broad indemnity (§ 12(a)). The single liability cap protects TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation and leaves Client uncapped — walk-away territory under the LOL-CAP rule.
- **Our data is licensed away.** § 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to distribute, license, resell and exploit borrower Credit Data independently of service delivery, and the Agreement contains no ownership or assignment of work product and no data-return or transition mechanic on exit.
- **Basic vendor protections are missing.** There is no conformance or services warranty (only a Year 2000 warranty in § 9), no insurance obligation of any kind, and no successor/M&A transfer right for either the Agreement or the licence.

Commercially, the minimum monthly fee floor in § 5(a) is a take-or-pay commitment that § 6 expressly insulates from documentation and challenge. Positive terms worth preserving: Client's unconditional exit right (§ 14), the 30-day non-renewal window and one-year renewal terms (§ 13), TrueLink's rate MFN and first-year price freeze (§ 6), Client's express freedom to use alternative suppliers (§ 2(a)), the absence of any audit, non-compete, non-solicit or liquidated-damages obligation on Client, and California law with California venue (§§ 26–27) — accepted at fallback.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 12(b) covers only TrueLink's own breach: no duty to defend, no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct indemnity, against a very broad Client indemnity in § 12(a). Add Vendor defend-and-indemnify (notice, control of defence, cooperation) covering Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data; narrow our indemnity to Client Content and our own breach of law. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | § 8(d) licenses TrueLink to distribute, resell and exploit borrower Credit Data beyond service delivery (walk-away); no ownership/assignment of work product. Narrow the licence to service delivery and add a Client ownership clause with licence back to embedded TrueLink IP. § 2(d) TrueLink platform IP preserved. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | Cap protects TrueLink only (12 months' hosting/support compensation); Client, including under § 12(a), is uncapped — walk-away. Make the existing §§ 3/4/7/11 cap mutual ("EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY") and extend the carve-out mutually to indemnification and confidentiality (§ 10) alongside gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 15 requires consent with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard. Seek Client-side affiliate and successor assignment without approval; TrueLink assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor; confirm no termination on Client change of control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No exclusivity on Client; § 2(a) licence is non-exclusive and expressly preserves our freedom to acquire or develop alternatives. § 3(i) is a sourcing condition on voluntary Interface use only. Preferred position; no redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination charge on Client (§§ 13, 14 exits are fee-free; § 5 fees are ordinary monthly consideration). Preferred position; resist any later termination fee above three months' fees. |
| High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Client. Noted: § 8(d) cross-refers to an unattached "Non-Competition Agreement" which there limits TrueLink only — review that side agreement separately. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 14 gives Client an unconditional no-cause exit (run-off to month-end following notice), no exit fee; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. At or above fallback. No pro-rata refund language, but fees are not prepaid (§ 5(a), monthly invoicing, 15 days). |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No audit or inspection right binding Client anywhere; § 6 verification runs in our favour. We will not insert audit parameters, as doing so would create a right that does not exist. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 26 California law; § 27 exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County, California; no arbitration. Fallback position — accepted, not redlined. |
| Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE | Grant runs to Client only, with no affiliate coverage and no successor transfer right (§ 15). Extend the licence to Client affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to an M&A successor without approval, drafted as an exception in § 15. |
| Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | The only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6 rate MFN plus one-year price freeze); no MFN burdens Client. Preferred position — preserve as drafted. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Deviation | § 5 COMPENSATION | § 5(a) imposes unconditional minimum monthly fees regardless of usage, recurring each renewal term (§ 13), and § 6 removes any right to documentation or to contest them. No reduction right and no true-up. Delete the fee floor and conform the § 6 carve-outs. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere. Preferred position; no redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 13: one-year renewal terms with a 30-day mutual non-renewal notice; no unilateral uplift (Exhibits A/B, § 6 freeze and MFN, § 16 written-amendment requirement). Meets fallback and most of preferred; absence of a 60-day renewal reminder noted only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No data return, export, migration assistance or deletion obligation (§§ 13, 14 place migration burdens on Client; § 10 has no return-or-destroy). Insert preferred clause: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter; fallback of 90 days / 30-day export offered in comment. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | TrueLink's only warranty is the § 9 Year 2000 warranty; no conformance or services warranty and no remedy. Insert fallback warranty: 90-day software conformance to documentation, 30-day services warranty, repair/replace or refund. The § 12 disclaimer is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so no consequential edit is needed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance obligation anywhere, although TrueLink hosts our Web Site and transmits consumer credit data. Insert a new Section 31: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M where TrueLink processes Client data, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away (or, for indemnity, close to walk-away) territory. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **One-way liability cap (§ 12).** TrueLink capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while Client's liability, including the broad § 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited. Minimum acceptable outcome: the existing cap made mutual, with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **Independent exploitation of borrower Credit Data (§ 8(d)).** The worldwide right to distribute, license, resell and exploit our Credit Data must be narrowed to what is needed to deliver the Services.
3. **No data return on exit.** Client Content ownership without any return, export or deletion mechanic. A transition and data-return clause must be added.
4. **No insurance of any kind**, in a relationship where TrueLink hosts our site and transmits consumer credit data.
5. **No Vendor IP or data-breach indemnity and no duty to defend**, set against a very broad Client indemnity — close to walk-away and the reason we are pressing the preferred position rather than a fallback.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six items requiring change: indemnity (§ 12), ownership and the Credit Data licence (§ 8(d)), the mutual liability cap (§ 12), assignment and licence transfer (§ 15 / § 2), minimum monthly fees (§ 5(a) and conforming § 6 edits), warranty, transition/data return and the new insurance section.
2. **Sequence the negotiation:** treat the mutual cap, the Vendor indemnity, the Credit Data licence, data return and insurance as the priority set; the licence-scope and assignment edits are drafted as narrow exceptions and should be presentable as clean-up.
3. **Commercial input needed** on the § 5(a) minimum monthly fee floors — confirm whether removal is achievable or whether we should instead seek a reduction right on 30 days' notice plus a true-up as the fallback.
4. **Obtain and review the "Non-Competition Agreement"** cross-referenced in § 8(d); it is undefined and unattached, and we need to confirm it contains no covenant binding Client.
5. **Preserve on our side** the § 14 exit right, § 13 renewal mechanics, the § 6 MFN and price freeze, § 2(a) freedom to use alternatives, the absence of any audit, non-solicit, non-compete or liquidated-damages obligation, and §§ 26–27 governing law and venue at fallback. We are not opening these.
6. **File notes for a future round:** no 60-day renewal reminder; no USD 1,000,000 cap floor, "paid or payable" formulation or mutual consequential-loss exclusion; no express pro-rata refund on convenience termination; and the audit parameters we would hold to if TrueLink later seeks usage verification."}
